column1: Special Case 1: The Classical Closed Economy Suppose that EP 5 P, L(i, Y ) 5 (1/V )Y, and CF(r – r∗) 5 0. In words, these equations mean that expectations of the price level adjust so that expectations are correct, money demand is proportional to income, and there are no international capital flows. In this case, output is always at its natural level, the real interest rate adjusts to equilibrate the goods market, the price level moves parallel with the money supply, and the nominal interest rate adjusts one-for-one with expected inflation. This special case corresponds to the economy analyzed in Chapters 3 and 5.
